name: VTFF (Visual Transformers with Feature Fusion)
authors_or_creators: Fuyan Ma, Bin Sun, Shutao Li (Hunan University, College of Electrical and Information Engineering)
publication_venue: IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing (2023); preprint arXiv 2021
backbone: Two-branch CNN (ResNet-18 / IR-50 stem producing LANet attentional feature maps) fused via a Visual Transformer encoder
accuracy_fer2013: [uncertain] (not the primary benchmark reported in the paper)
accuracy_affectnet: 61.85% (7-class, Overall/WAR) [uncertain on UAR vs WAR specifics]
hardware_requirements: Trained on a single NVIDIA GPU (Tesla V100/Titan-class) [uncertain on exact configuration]; inference feasible on a single mid-range GPU
loss_function: Standard softmax cross-entropy classification loss over expression categories
training_data_used: Trained and evaluated separately on RAF-DB, FERPlus, and AffectNet; CNN backbone initialized from MS-Celeb-1M / face-recognition pretraining
pretraining_strategy: face-recognition-pretrain (CNN backbone pretrained on large-scale face recognition data); transformer fusion module trained from scratch with end-to-end fine-tuning
pretraining_corpus: MS-Celeb-1M (face recognition pretraining for the CNN backbone) [uncertain]
input_modality: RGB image (single static face crop, typically 112x112 or 224x224)
cross_dataset_generalization: [uncertain] (cross-dataset transfer not a primary focus of the paper)
robustness: Reports improved robustness to occlusion and pose variation thanks to the Attentional Selective Fusion (ASF) module that adaptively weights local-global features; evaluated qualitatively rather than on standard Occlusion/Pose-RAF-DB splits [uncertain on exact numbers]
explainability: Attention map visualization from the visual transformer; LANet attentional feature maps highlight discriminative facial regions
